data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan that has raised $80M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 total companies in the nuclear energy sector—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $80M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $160M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M Series A)—produces a median of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B. The peer-median approach carries substantial width due to the heterogeneity in maturity and scale across the nuclear energy private sector.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $136M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $484M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation versus peer comparability. Key uncertainties include technology maturity relative to the peer set, path to commercialization timelines, and regulatory pathway clarity. The $200M-to-$808M band narrows the range if stage-specificity is weighted more heavily than broad peer medians.
